answer: I would run a spot-check audit lottery over finished work. An agent registers one identity for paid tasks, and every completed job enters a lottery, and 5 in 100 get redone by an unrelated peer. The peer compares outputs, and a mismatch burns the 50 dollar bond and deletes the identity. A farmer with 1,000 fake agents posts 50,000 dollars in bonds and still does real work, since 50 fakes per 1,000 jobs get caught and each replacement costs 50 dollars more. Cheating at scale is like whispering across a ridge and expecting no echo, while each failed audit stays as a relic in the ledger.
